title: Optimizing Internal Knowledge Retrieval for Technical Support
business: Enterprise technical support teams managing large internal documentation repositories.
problem: Support agents struggle to find relevant technical documentation quickly, leading to increased resolution times and inconsistent answers due to keyword-based search limitations.
solution: Implementing bge-small-en-v1.5 as a feature-extraction model to convert technical documentation into dense vector embeddings, enabling semantic search that understands the intent behind agent queries rather than just matching keywords.
steps: Pre-process internal technical documents into manageable text chunks.
Initialize the bge-small-en-v1.5 model to generate vector representations for each document chunk.
Store the resulting embeddings in a vector database for efficient similarity searching.
Convert incoming agent queries into vector embeddings using the same model.
Perform a cosine similarity search between the query vector and the document vectors to retrieve the most relevant technical passages.
outcome: Support agents receive contextually accurate documentation snippets, significantly reducing the time spent navigating static knowledge bases.
limitation: The model produces a similarity distribution typically in the interval [0.6, 1.0], meaning that a score above 0.5 does not inherently imply high semantic similarity; developers must empirically determine a specific threshold (e.g., 0.85) based on their unique data distribution.
